claims.claim: The text expressly calls Jephthah's promised offering an olah (burnt offering)
claims.evidence: Judges 11:31 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The text expressly calls the promised offering an olah (burnt offering). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Literal sacrifice is a substantial reading of Judges 11:30–40; perpetual dedication is an alternate interpretation. The passage says he did to her according to his vow, without describing the killing scene.
claims.evidence: Judges 11:30–40 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). The passage says he did to her according to his vow, without describing the killing scene. The substantial/alternate weighting rests on Kočí (Open Theology 2021) and Reiss (Louvain Studies 2012), both read only at abstract level; neither enters sources[]. Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

claims.claim: Judges 12:5–6 depicts a shibboleth-based identification at Jordan fords
claims.evidence: Judges 12:5–6 (Hebrew Bible, Judges 1–21, Masoretic text, read in full in Hebrew and JPS English via Mechon Mamre). Textual description only; the narrated event is not externally corroborated.

connections.note: Amorite and Transjordan land history used in Jephthah's speech (Numbers 21:21–35). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
Prohibition of child sacrifice in normative law (Deuteronomy 12:31). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
Contrasting narrative of a child offered but spared (Genesis 22:1–19). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.
Later canonical recollection of Jephthah by name (Hebrews 11:32). This is a literary/thematic relation, not an independently verified shared historical event.

review.notes: Proposed unpublished Judges category; source access remains limited and audit restrictions apply. Phase 4 readiness and independent QA are distinct. No editorial override needed: S001 and Josephus in sources[] are verified; S025 was narrowed out (2026-11-23, per the S009/S025 evaluation §3.2) — the two prose sentences citing it (Ammonite core-territory geography around Amman, east of the Jordan; the earliest evidence naming the Ammonites is ninth-century BCE) were deleted (the Amman parenthetical dropped from the first, the ninth-century clause and its dating-evidence tail deleted from the second), so the claims survive on S001 alone and no S025-dependent prose remains. The full annotated bibliography is behind an access wall and cannot be read from this VM, so completing the read is not achievable here; the narrowing removes the override question entirely. No override is needed for in-review (the override rule applies to published records). S001 ENTERS sources[] even though the prose cites no [^S001] inline (the only 'S001' in the draft is the Source Notes entry): JCL-08-001 lists S001;S017 and JCL-08-003 lists S001 alone, and the claims are textual-description claims grounded in the biblical text; excluding S001 would leave JCL-08-003 with NO source in sources[] at all. S017 and S018 do NOT enter sources[] (EM-directed hard line): S017 (Kočí, Open Theology 2021) and S018 (Reiss, Louvain Studies 2012) are both not-independently-verified and abstract-only (S017: DOAJ abstract read, De Gruyter full text HTTP 405, not read; S018: abstract + bibliographic details read, 106-page body not read, paywalled/registration), and they are defined-but-uncited inline (they appear only in the Source Notes — no [^S017]/[^S018] in the prose). They are the registry sources for JCL-08-001 (S017) and JCL-08-002 (S017;S018) but do not enter sources[]; JCL-08-002's textual-description limb ("The passage says he did to her according to his vow, without describing the killing scene") is grounded by S001, and the claim is debated, signalling the interpretation is disputed. S026 is not listed in sources[] — it is cited in the registry for the connections, but claims and connections carry no per-item source lists in the category JSON (J01/J02/J03/J04/J05/J06/J07 precedent); the J08 draft cites no S026 footnote. JCL-08-004 is EXCLUDED from this category (J02/JCL-02-003 precedent): its registry final_editorial_instruction is "EXCLUDE from published factual claims; retain audit ID and rationale" — the 300-year claim is not independent material dating evidence. The prose discussion of the 300-year claim stays as-is (it presents it as part of the speech's argument, not as a factual claim). JADD-006 does NOT apply to J08: the additional-items-review labels JADD-006 as "J12, Judg 20:18,26–28" (Bethel/KJV rendering note; 5-way split 20:1; 20:18; 20:26–28; 21:12; 21:19 — never build as 20:18–28). Judges 20–21 is J12's territory, not J08's (Judg 11–12). No Judg 20–21 split is built into J08. No internal research IDs (JCL-/JADD-) appear in the reader-facing prose (the draft already contained none), and the prose is kept precise to what the claims state (the 300 years is an argument inside a diplomatic message, not a date; the shibboleth is a single test at a single crossing, not a map of dialects; neither reading of the vow is chosen). The D7 guard ("Both readings must therefore be presented, and neither is chosen in this article") stays verbatim.
